chapter: The Paradise and life in Queens
title: Reading the Koran; friends who changed names
summary: Idrees Sulieman gave him the Koran but he declined to change names; he stayed friends with Sadik Hakim and drummer Kalil Madi.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: that people had about that at that time?
Well they did. I read the Koran and...
Who gave that to you to read?

I think it was Idrees Sulieman. His name was Graham before that. But we were friends , we were with Sabby Lewis, you know, and when he became involved with that I listened, because, you know, I listen to everybody. And I saw the good points, but I says, "I been thinkin', you have to change your children's names and your social security card and everything's got to be changed and you gotta get your name changed legally and your children become somethin' else, different names, and they got to live through all that." And, you know, I saw all that and I says, "No. That's too much, " you know. It's all right for them, but not for me. You know, it's different strokes for different folks, you know. But everybody's still
friends, you know, we're still friends. Yeah. But they approached me with that, yeah. And Sadik, you know, the piano player.

Yeah, sure, and we're still friends. I saw him last time I was in here, in New York, he came by to see me in several places, you know, at the Tin Palace, he came by the West End. Still the same guy like when we first saw each other, you know. Oh, then Kalil, the drummer, he worked with me at the Paradise, after Tim Kennedy left. And he changed his name too. But we're still friends. I haven't seen him.
Yeah, Jimmy Cobb has spoken well of him.
